clouds.title: Clouds
clouds.intro: What you see out of the window when the ground disappears, and what each cloud means for your flight.

entries.title: Cumulus
entries.short: Puffy, cotton-wool clouds with flat bases
entries.what: Heaps of cloud built by rising warm air on sunny days. Their flat bases all sit at the same height, where the air cools enough for water to condense.
entries.plane: From above they look like scattered popcorn over the land, each with its own shadow on the ground.
entries.flight: Small bumps while climbing or descending through them. Above them the ride is usually smooth.

entries.title: Towering cumulus
entries.short: Tall, cauliflower-topped towers
entries.what: Cumulus that keep growing upward on strong rising air, with hard, bright, bubbling tops. Many grow into thunderstorms.
entries.plane: Tall white towers rising above the rest of the clouds, often in a line.
entries.flight: Pilots steer around them because the air inside is rough. If the seatbelt sign comes on near them, that is why.

entries.title: Cumulonimbus
entries.short: The thunderstorm cloud, with a flat anvil top
entries.what: The biggest cloud of all, reaching from near the ground to 12 km or more. Its top spreads into a flat anvil where it hits the stable air above.
entries.plane: A huge white mountain with a flat, spreading top. At night, lightning flickers inside it, often silently.
entries.flight: Aircraft go around these, sometimes by tens of kilometres; that is one reason the real route bends. Common during the monsoon and pre-monsoon storms.

entries.title: Stratocumulus
entries.short: A lumpy grey blanket of low cloud
entries.what: A low layer broken into rolls or patches, the most common cloud on Earth.
entries.plane: From above, a soft white or grey floor with gaps through which you glimpse the ground.
entries.flight: Light bumps passing through it; a smooth ride once above.

entries.title: Stratus and fog
entries.short: A flat, featureless grey layer, sometimes on the ground
entries.what: A uniform low sheet of cloud. When it touches the ground it is fog.
entries.plane: A flat white sea with nothing showing through. Hills and tall buildings sometimes poke out of it.
entries.flight: Winter fog over the north Indian plains is a big cause of delays at Delhi, Lucknow and other airports, where landings then need special instrument approaches.

entries.title: Altocumulus
entries.short: Rows or patches of small rounded clouds, higher up
entries.what: Mid-level clouds, roughly 2 to 6 km up, often arranged in neat rows or a dappled pattern.
entries.plane: Patterned layers you climb through after take-off, or see below you at cruise.
entries.flight: Usually a smooth ride. Seen in the morning on a humid day, they can mean storms later.

entries.title: Altostratus
entries.short: A grey veil that dims the sun
entries.what: A thin to thick mid-level sheet. The sun shows through it as if through frosted glass.
entries.plane: A grey, even layer that hides the ground, with no shape to it.
entries.flight: Often arrives ahead of a large rain system. A smooth but dull ride inside it.

entries.title: Nimbostratus
entries.short: Thick, dark rain cloud
entries.what: A deep layer of cloud that brings steady, long-lasting rain, typical of the monsoon's wet days.
entries.plane: After take-off you stay in grey for a long time, with rain streaking across the window.
entries.flight: Mostly a steady ride, but slow, grey climbs and descents. Wet runways can mean longer landing rolls.

entries.title: Cirrus
entries.short: High, wispy streaks of ice
entries.what: Thin, feathery clouds made of ice crystals, 8 km or more up, often drawn out into hooks or 'mares' tails' by strong winds.
entries.plane: At cruising height they can be level with you or just above, like streaks of white paint.
entries.flight: Usually smooth. Long streaks can show a jet stream nearby, which sometimes brings light turbulence.

entries.title: Cirrostratus
entries.short: A thin high sheet that makes a halo
entries.what: A transparent veil of ice crystals covering the sky. It often makes a ring of light, a halo, around the sun or moon.
entries.plane: A faint milky haze above or around you; look for the halo.
entries.flight: A smooth ride. On the ground it can mean rain within a day.

entries.title: Cirrocumulus
entries.short: Tiny high ripples, like fish scales
entries.what: Small, high, grainy clouds in rows or ripples, sometimes called a mackerel sky.
entries.plane: A delicate rippled pattern, sometimes at your height at cruise.
entries.flight: Smooth. They are short-lived and quite rare.

entries.title: Lenticular clouds
entries.short: Smooth lens shapes near mountains
entries.what: Saucer-shaped clouds that form where strong wind flows over mountains and sets up waves in the air downwind.
entries.plane: Smooth, stacked lenses that seem to hang still, near the Himalaya and other high ranges.
entries.flight: They mark mountain waves, which can bring turbulence. Pilots treat them with respect.

entries.title: Contrails
entries.short: White lines left by other aircraft
entries.what: Trails of ice crystals formed when hot, wet engine exhaust meets the very cold air at cruising height.
entries.plane: Look for another aircraft drawing a white line across the sky, often far above or below you.
entries.flight: Short trails that fade quickly mean dry air up high; long ones that spread out mean the upper air is humid.

entries.title: Glory
entries.short: A rainbow ring around your plane's shadow
entries.what: A set of coloured rings formed when sunlight is scattered back by tiny cloud droplets, centred on the point exactly opposite the sun.
entries.plane: When the sun is behind you and there is cloud below, look for the plane's shadow on the cloud: it may sit inside a small rainbow circle.
entries.flight: Pure luck and a great photo. Sit on the side away from the sun to see it.

entries.title: Haze and smog
entries.short: A brown layer that hides the ground
entries.what: Dust, smoke and pollution held near the ground, often under a lid of warmer air.
entries.plane: Climbing out you pass through a brownish layer, then above it the sky turns clear blue. Looking down, the ground fades into it.
entries.flight: Over the north Indian plains in winter, haze and smog can hide the ground for much of the flight.

land.title: India from the air
land.intro: Patterns you can actually see from 35,000 feet, what makes them, and where in India to look.

entries.title: Indo-Gangetic Plain
entries.short: A flat patchwork of fields to the horizon
entries.what: One of the largest and most fertile plains on Earth, built from silt carried down from the Himalaya by the Ganges, the Indus and their tributaries.
entries.plane: Small fields in every shade of green and brown, villages every few kilometres, winding rivers and, in winter, a lot of haze.
entries.where: Most flights from Delhi, Lucknow, Patna or Kolkata spend a long time over it.

entries.title: Brick kilns
entries.short: Oval rings with a tall chimney, by the thousand
entries.what: Traditional brick kilns, built as long oval trenches with a single chimney, fired with coal and agricultural waste.
entries.plane: Small dark ovals scattered across the fields near towns, often with a plume of smoke from the chimney.
entries.where: All over the Gangetic plains in the dry season, especially in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Punjab.

entries.title: Meanders and oxbow lakes
entries.short: Rivers that loop back on themselves
entries.what: On flat land rivers swing from side to side. Sometimes a loop is cut off, leaving a curved lake called an oxbow.
entries.plane: Snake-like rivers and curved, crescent-shaped lakes or green scars beside them where old channels used to run.
entries.where: Along the Ganges, Ghaghara, Gandak and Kosi across the northern plains.

entries.title: Braided rivers
entries.short: Many channels weaving across a wide sandy bed
entries.what: Rivers carrying a lot of sand and gravel split into many channels that wander between sandbars, called chars in the east.
entries.plane: A very wide, pale bed with silver threads of water weaving through it. In the monsoon it can become one huge sheet of water.
entries.where: The Brahmaputra in Assam, the Kosi in Bihar, and rivers coming out of the Himalaya.

entries.title: Chambal ravines
entries.short: Badlands of deep gullies
entries.what: Soft soil along the Chambal and Yamuna has been cut by rain and floods into a maze of deep, steep-sided gullies.
entries.plane: Wrinkled, brown, finger-like land along the rivers, with almost no fields, quite unlike the flat farmland around it.
entries.where: Where Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh meet, on routes south from Delhi.

entries.title: Aravalli Range
entries.short: Low, rocky, ancient hills
entries.what: Among the oldest mountains on Earth, worn down over a very long time into low, rocky ridges.
entries.plane: Lines of brown, rocky hills running south-west from near Delhi, with dry scrub and lakes trapped between ridges.
entries.where: Between Delhi and Gujarat, especially near Udaipur and Mount Abu.

entries.title: Thar Desert
entries.short: Dunes and scattered villages
entries.what: The Great Indian Desert, a dry region of sand dunes, rocky plains and salt lakes.
entries.plane: Beige land with ripples of dunes, ring-shaped villages and very few fields, crossed by long straight roads.
entries.where: Western Rajasthan; flights to Jodhpur, Jaisalmer and Bikaner, and some routes to the Gulf.

entries.title: Indira Gandhi Canal
entries.short: A straight green line through the desert
entries.what: One of the longest canals in India, bringing Himalayan river water deep into the Thar Desert.
entries.plane: A thin straight line of water with a green belt of fields along it, sharp against the sand.
entries.where: Northern and western Rajasthan, from near the Punjab border towards Jaisalmer.

entries.title: Deccan Traps
entries.short: Flat-topped hills with stepped sides
entries.what: Thick layers of basalt laid down by huge volcanic eruptions around 66 million years ago. 'Trap' comes from a Swedish word for stairs.
entries.plane: Flat-topped hills and plateaus whose sides drop in steps, each step a separate lava flow.
entries.where: Western Maharashtra and the north-western Deccan; routes around Mumbai, Pune and Nashik.

entries.title: Western Ghats
entries.short: A green wall of hills along the west coast
entries.what: A long mountain chain running parallel to the west coast, catching the monsoon rain. A UNESCO World Heritage Site and a biodiversity hotspot.
entries.plane: A steep, deep green escarpment with the narrow coastal plain and the sea on one side and the drier plateau on the other.
entries.where: Flights to Goa, Mangaluru, Kochi or between Mumbai and Bengaluru.

entries.title: Rann of Kutch
entries.short: A dazzling white salt desert
entries.what: A huge seasonal salt marsh. It floods in the monsoon, then dries into a flat crust of white salt.
entries.plane: In the dry months, a vast blinding-white flat with no features at all.
entries.where: Northern Gujarat; flights to Bhuj and some routes towards the Gulf.

entries.title: Salt pans
entries.short: Coloured rectangles along the coast
entries.what: Shallow ponds where seawater is left to evaporate to make salt. Algae turn some of them pink, red or green.
entries.plane: Neat grids of rectangles in white, pink and brown at the edge of the sea.
entries.where: Gujarat's coast, around Mumbai, and Tamil Nadu near Thoothukudi.

entries.title: Fish and shrimp ponds
entries.short: Grids of rectangular ponds near the coast
entries.what: Ponds dug for farming fish and shrimp, which have replaced rice fields across many river deltas.
entries.plane: Hundreds of dark, water-filled rectangles packed together like a chessboard.
entries.where: The Godavari and Krishna deltas in Andhra Pradesh, and coastal Odisha and West Bengal.

entries.title: Tanks of the south
entries.short: Thousands of small irregular lakes
entries.what: Small reservoirs made by building an earth bank across a slope to catch the monsoon rain, some of them centuries old.
entries.plane: The land is dotted with small lakes of every shape, often chained together down a slope, full and blue after the monsoon.
entries.where: Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Telangana, especially on approach to Bengaluru and Hyderabad.

entries.title: Terraced fields
entries.short: Steps cut into hillsides
entries.what: Flat steps built into steep slopes so they can be farmed without the soil washing away.
entries.plane: Hillsides lined with thin curving contour lines, like a map's elevation lines drawn on the ground.
entries.where: The Himalayan foothills, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim and the north-east.

entries.title: Tea gardens
entries.short: Neat green carpets with scattered shade trees
entries.what: Large estates of tea bushes clipped to waist height, with tall trees planted among them for shade.
entries.plane: Smooth, bright green blocks with a fine dotted texture and straight estate roads, very different from ordinary fields.
entries.where: Assam's Brahmaputra valley, the Dooars and Darjeeling in West Bengal, and the Nilgiris.

entries.title: Sundarbans
entries.short: A maze of mangrove islands
entries.what: The largest mangrove forest in the world, on the delta of the Ganges and Brahmaputra; home to the Bengal tiger. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.
entries.plane: Dark green islands cut by countless winding creeks and wide brown channels running into the sea.
entries.where: South of Kolkata, towards the Bay of Bengal.

entries.title: The Himalaya
entries.short: Snow peaks along the horizon
entries.what: The highest mountain range on Earth, still rising as India pushes into Asia.
entries.plane: On clear days a line of snow peaks stands above the haze along the northern horizon, sometimes more than 200 km away.
entries.where: Northern side of flights across the Gangetic plain; best on clear winter mornings, on the side facing north.

entries.title: Open-cast mines
entries.short: Grey pits and terraces in the forest
entries.what: Huge open pits dug to reach coal or iron ore near the surface.
entries.plane: Grey or black terraced pits with dumps of spoil around them, cut into green forest.
entries.where: Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh.

entries.title: Cities at night
entries.short: Orange glow and lit highways
entries.what: Street lights, homes and roads seen together from above.
entries.plane: Big cities show as bright orange blobs with glowing highways leading out like spokes. Small towns are a scatter of faint dots in the dark.
entries.where: Any night flight; the Gangetic plain is a carpet of small lights, and big cities like Delhi and Mumbai glow on the horizon long before you reach them.
